answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities sign conflicting claims, correlated penalties grow as O(k²), rather than merely adding a fixed charge per identity. Detection slashes bonded collateral and applies asymmetric capital depreciation, so losses compound across the swarm and can create an exponential multiplier in capital loss. A harbor, voyage, and beacon may guide honest participation, but splitting one operator across identities does not dilute shared evidence or its penalty.
